question: Under the proposed National Building Research Institute law, how long does an employee have to decide whether to decline the offered position after being notified?
answer:
Under the National Building Research Institute Bill, the opt-out window is "within six months from the date on which he was offered employment in the Institute" [629/2025 §33(2)(b)]; the same clause appears verbatim in the Gazette version [621/2025 §33(2)(b)], so the two versions do not differ.

- The trigger is the date the offer was made, not a separate notification date — no distinct "notification" deadline appears in the text [629/2025 §33(2)(b)].
- Employees who decline are paid compensation under a voluntary retirement scheme approved by the Minister and the Minister of Finance [629/2025 §33(2)(c)].

Caveats: The passage is extracted from §33 only; it does not address what happens if the six-month period lapses without a decision, and I cannot confirm from this evidence whether other clauses set a different or additional deadline.

question: Under the proposed Inland Revenue amendment, from which assessment date are deductions previously claimed under sections 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act excluded from subsection (2)?
answer:
Deductions previously claimed under sections 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act are excluded where they relate to “any year of assessment prior to April 1, 2018” [013/2026 §37].

- This applies even if an un-deducted balance of that deduction remains as at April 1, 2018 [013/2026 §37].
- Source is the Inland Revenue (Amendment) Bill, GS, 2026-02-24; identical text appears in 022/2026 [013/2026 §37].

question: Under the proposed Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority law, how long does a licence issued or renewed remain in effect?
answer:
Under the Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority bill, a licence issued under section 23 or renewed under section 24 is valid for **one year** [645/2025 §25(c)].

- It must also specify its expiry date and is non-transferable [645/2025 §25(d)-(e)].
- It is subject to an annual licence fee set by the Authority [645/2025 §25(b)].
- Separately, a licence to carry on the **microfinance business** under section 32 is stated to be issued “for a period of three years” [645/2025 §32(7)].

Caveat: the evidence is the GS version dated 2025-11-17, with identical text in 653/2025.

question: How far in advance must a container depot operator lodge a renewal request before the current licence ends?
answer:
A container depot operator must submit the renewal application **not less than thirty days prior** to the current licence’s expiration date [657/2025 §6(1)].

- The application must be in the prescribed Form and accompanied by the prescribed renewal fee [657/2025 §6(1)].
- The evidence notes this text is identical in Bill 007/2026 [657/2025 §6].

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, what is the new maximum duration a freezing order may be in effect?
answer:
Under the newest version, Bill 033/2026 (2026-05-05; identical text in GS 020/2026, 2026-03-17), the s.8(2)(b) cap rises to **“shall not exceed four months”** from three months, and the separate **“period of two years”** becomes **“three years”** [033/2026 §9].

- The initial police Freezing Order period is separately extended to **“fourteen working days”** [033/2026 §8].
- Caveat: the extract does not give the full s.8(2) wording, so “three years” appears to be the outer period rather than a single order’s length.

question: Under the amended Telecommunication Levy law, how often is the levy calculated on the value of telecom services received?
Under the amended Bills of Exchange Ordinance, what ways are allowed for informing a party that a bill has been refused or not paid?
answer:
The amended section 49(5) allows notice of dishonour to be given "in writing or by personal communication, or by facsimile transmission or other electronic means" [601/2025 §8].

- The electronic/fax route requires the means to "sufficiently identify the bill, and intimate that the bill has been dishonoured by non-acceptance or non-payment" [601/2025 §8].
- The provision substitutes a new subsection (5) of section 49 of the principal enactment (Chapter 82) [601/2025 §8].
- Per that passage the same text appears in the newer Bill 612/2025 (2025-06-17) and in 527/2024 / 552/2024 [601/2025 §8].

Caveats: The clause text is quoted from the GS version 601/2025 (2025-06-04); the Bill 612/2025 is described there as identical, but no separate clause text for it is in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed Kodhagoda Gunarathana Nahimi Foundation incorporation law, who is defined as a qualified auditor?
answer:
Under §11(4) of the Bill, a "qualified auditor" is either an individual member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka (or any other Institute established by law) holding "a certified to practice as Accountant issued by the Council of such Institute", or a firm of accountants whose resident partners each meet that same membership-and-certificate requirement [626/2025 §11(4)]. The auditor is appointed by the Auditor General under Article 154 of the Constitution [626/2025 §11(3)].

- Individual: member of the Institute with a practising certificate from its Council [626/2025 §11(4)(a)].
- Firm: every resident partner must be such a member with such a certificate [626/2025 §11(4)(b)].

Caveats: The wording "a certified to practice as Accountant" is quoted as it appears in the text; the passage is identical in Bill 607/2025, and only this Bill version (not a GS version) is in evidence.

question: What is meant by “knowledge sharing activities” under the Sri Lanka Institute of Agriculture Act?
answer:
The definition appears in the interpretation clause: “knowledge sharing activities” means “activities designed to facilitate to exchange of ideas, skills, and experiences fostering on culture of learning and collaboration” [646/2025 §18] (quoted as printed, including its typos).

- It is a definitions-only provision, so the meaning is limited to that phrase [646/2025 §18].
- The same text appears in 002/2026, per the evidence note [646/2025 §18].

Caveats: This is the Gazette version (GS, 2025-11-20) of the “Sri Lanka Institute of Agriculture (Incorporation)” bill — not an enacted Act — and the quoted wording is garbled, so the intended meaning (“facilitate the exchange… fostering a culture…”) is my reading, not the text’s.

question: According to the proposed Pharmaceutical Society of Sri Lanka law, what authority does the Society have to obtain and manage real or personal assets, and what actions may it take with those assets?
answer:
The Society may take and hold any movable or immovable property vested in it and may sell, mortgage, lease, exchange or otherwise dispose of it [047/2026 §13]. The GS version (2026-06-11) is identical on this clause [041/2026 §13].

- Property may vest by “purchase, grant, gift, testamentary disposition or otherwise” and is held for the Act’s purposes, subject to s.7 rules [047/2026 §13].
- It may also purchase, rent, construct, renovate or otherwise obtain land/buildings and dispose of them as the Council determines [047/2026 §6(a)].
- It may administer trusts over “any real or personal property” to promote its objects [047/2026 §6(f)]; s.7 rules must cover property administration and management [047/2026 §7(1)(f)].

question: In the Institute of Real Estate Professionals, who chairs the Membership and Policy Advisory committees, and how are chairs selected for the remaining committees?
answer:
The President of the Institute chairs the Membership Committee and the Policy Advisory and Constitutional Committee; for the other committees, a Council member on the committee is Chairman, or the Council picks one if several Council members are appointed.

- "the President of the Institute shall be the Chairman of the Committees referred to in paragraphs (a) and (b)" — i.e. Membership (a) and Policy Advisory and Constitutional (b) [656/2025 §18(2)], same in the GS [637/2025 §18(2)].
- Every other committee must include "at least, one member of the Council and such member shall be the Chairman" [656/2025 §18(2)].
- Where more than one Council member sits on a committee, "the Council shall appoint one of such members as the Chairperson" [656/2025 §18(3)].

Caveat: the bill names it the "Policy Advisory and Constitutional Committee", not simply "Policy Advisory"; the Bill (2025-12-05) and GS (2025-10-01) texts are identical here.

question: Under the amended Colombo Port City Economic Commission law, how is the income tax treatment of workers hired by licensed businesses affected depending on whether the licence was granted before or after the new provisions take effect?
answer:
Under the newest version, **Bill 654/2025** (Colombo Port City Economic Commission (Amendment) – Bill, 2025-12-05; same clause in **GS 652/2025**, 2025-11-28), pre-commencement licensees’ employees get a three-year income-tax exemption, while employees of licensees granted on/after commencement are taxable.

- Pre-commencement licensee: resident employee’s employment income is “exempt from income tax” and deemed a permissible credit to a personal foreign currency account; non-resident employee’s employment income is exempt, and they are not liable to Sri Lankan income tax on foreign-earned income [654/2025 §3; 652/2025 §3].
- The exemption is “for a period of three years” from the month after the section commences [654/2025 §3].
- Post-commencement licensee: resident and non-resident employees’ employment income “shall be liable to income tax” [654/2025 §3].

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders, Non‑Vessel Operating Common Carriers and Container Operators Act, how is the Act’s long title changed regarding the mention of container operators?
answer:
In the newest Bill 005/2026 (20 Jan 2026; same text as GS 658/2025, 12 Dec 2025), the long title is amended by substituting “freight forwarders and non-vessel operating common carriers” for the phrase that includes “container operators”, thereby removing the container-operators reference [658/2025 §2] (identical text also in 005/2026).

- The resulting Act name is “Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders and Non-Vessel Operating Common Carriers Act” [658/2025 §3(1)(a)] (identical text also in 005/2026).

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, what modification is being made to the existing law?
answer:
It amends **section 3** of the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, No. 25 of 2005, mainly by widening the fault element and adding modes of liability and a new offence [029/2026 §4].

- The proviso to s.3(1) is replaced so that for an act to constitute the offence "it shall not be necessary to show" that the funds were actually used in an offence or "linked to a specific terrorist act" [029/2026 §4(1)].
- s.3(2)(b) is replaced with "aids or abets the commission of", and new paragraphs (ba)–(bc) are inserted covering organising/directing, being an accomplice, and contributing [029/2026 §4(2)].
- A new s.3(2B) offence covers collecting or providing funds, property or other assets, or material support, knowing or having reason to believe they will be used to finance persons for terrorist training, travel to commit a terrorist act, or becoming a foreign terrorist fighter [029/2026 §4(3)].

Caveats: identical text appears in GS 018/2026 (2026-03-11) and Bill 029/2026 (2026-04-09); the Schedule also substitutes wording across several sections [029/2026].

question: Which 2025 bill outlines the government's budget and borrowing provisions for the financial year 2026?
answer:
The **Appropriation Bill 639/2025** (Bill, 26 Sept 2025) is the 2025 bill for FY2026 spending and borrowing. An earlier **632/2025** (17 Sept 2025) contains identical §2 text.

- It authorises estimated expenditure of “rupees four thousand four hundred thirty-four billion three hundred fifty-six million four hundred sixty-eight thousand” for 1 Jan–31 Dec 2026 [639/2025 §2].
- It authorises FY2026 borrowing, with outstanding balance not exceeding “rupees three thousand eight hundred billion,” reported under s.51 of the Public Financial Management Act [639/2025 §2].

Caveats: The evidence labels 632/2025 as “Appropriation (Other)” but only states §2 text is identical.

question: What 2026 legislation establishes a new foundation to promote economic growth and rural resource development in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The Economic and Rural Resources Development Foundation (Incorporation) Bill — Bill [055/2026] (presented 2026-07-27), previously published as GS [043/2026] (2026-06-15). Note it *incorporates an already existing* Foundation rather than creating a new one [043/2026 §2, p.2].

- Objects include developing "all economic sectors in Sri Lanka" and human resource programmes for rural youth [043/2026 §3(1)(a)-(b)].
- It also covers micro-entrepreneurship for unemployed women, drug-abuse prevention, and soil conservation [043/2026 §3(1)(f)-(i)].
- Implementation must be "without any distinction based on race, religion, language, caste, sex, political opinion, place of birth" [043/2026 §3(2)].

Caveats: The bill title misspells "Recourses" in [055/2026]; the clause text in [043/2026] reads "Resources".

question: Under the proposed Chartered Institute of Media law, what is the maximum length of a suspension the Council can impose instead of disenrolling a member?
answer:
The maximum suspension is **one year**.

- In lieu of disenrolling, the Council may “warn, reprimand or suspend him from membership for such period not exceeding one year” [054/2026 §24].

question: Under the Protection of Occupants Bill, how long must someone have continuously and peacefully occupied a premises to be regarded as an “occupant”?
answer:
More than three months: the person must be in "lawful occupation" and have had "undisturbed and uninterrupted occupation" of the premises "for a period of more than three months" before the events in sections 3, 4 or 5 [004/2026 §2].

- The wording is "undisturbed and uninterrupted", not "continuously and peacefully" as in your question [004/2026 §2].
- The earlier Gazette version uses the identical three-month test: "more than three months" [634/2025 §2] (Protection of Occupants - GS, 2025-09-18); the presented Bill is dated 2026-01-20 [004/2026 §2].

Caveats: none of the quoted text defines how interruptions are treated; only §§2–4 excerpts are in evidence.

question: Under the proposed Gambling Regulatory Authority law, what is the age limit beyond which a person cannot serve on the Authority's Board?
answer:
The evidence I have does state an age bar: a person is disqualified from appointment to the Board if they "is over seventy years of age" [613/2025 §9(i)]; the same clause appears in the Gazette version [594/2025 §9(i)].

- The disqualification is framed as a bar on being "appointed as a member of the Board", not expressly on continuing to serve [613/2025 §9].
- Both versions (GS 2025-05-27; Bill 2025-06-17) carry identical text on this point [594/2025 §9; 613/2025 §9].

Caveats: Only §9 is in evidence; nothing here states whether a member who turns 70 in office must vacate, and other provisions may exist that are not in the passages given.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Financial Transactions Reporting Act, what is the longest jail term a person can receive for arriving in or departing Sri Lanka with cash or bearer‑negotiable instruments above the minister‑set limit?
answer:
The maximum jail term is **one year**: “imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding one year,” on conviction by a Magistrate [021/2026 §31]. The same clause also allows a fine “not exceeding three times of the value” of the cash or bearer-negotiable instruments, or both [021/2026 §31].

- The offence applies where the amount exceeds the Minister-specified sum and was not first reported to the relevant authority [021/2026 §31].
- The text is marked identical in the presented Bill [030/2026] and the Gazette version [021/2026 §31].

question: Under the proposed Sri Lanka Cricket law, what penalty amount does a member owe if they fail to pay the subscription by the deadline?
answer:
A defaulting member owes a "late payment fee equal to twice the annual subscription", due "on or before the thirtieth day of April of the following year" [072/2026 §30(4)]; the subscription itself is due by 31 December of the preceding year [072/2026 §30(3)].

- Continuing default past that late-payment date means automatic forfeiture of voting rights [072/2026 §30(5)], and removal from the Register of Members if unpaid six months after the due date [072/2026 §30(6)].
- The same text appears in bill 077/2026 [072/2026 §30, header note].

Caveats: Only "twice the annual subscription" is specified — no fixed rupee figure; the subscription amount is set by rules [072/2026 §30(1)].

question: Under the proposed Indira Cancer Charitable Trust Act, on which day must the newly formed body corporate settle the Trust's existing debts and liabilities?
answer:
The evidence does not give a settlement deadline. It only identifies *which* debts: those "existing on the day immediately preceding the date of commencement of this Act," which "shall be paid by the body corporate hereby constituted" [009/2026 §12].

- No day, time limit or period for payment appears in that clause — it states an obligation, not a deadline [009/2026 §12].
- I rely on the newest matching bill, "Indira Cancer Charitable Trust (Incorporation)" — GS, 2026-02-05 (identical text also in 014/2026) [009/2026 §12].
- The 2021 bill "Indira Cancer Trust (Incorporation)" — GS, 2021-08-23, uses materially the same wording ("for the purpose of this Act") [095/2021 §12].

Caveats: No commencement date or payment timetable is in the evidence, so a specific day cannot be stated.

question: Under the proposed Immigration Bill, what is the minimum and maximum penalty imposed on a ship's master or aircraft captain who fails to report a transit passenger or crew member that appears to have stayed in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The penalty is a fine of "not less than one hundred thousand rupees and not more than five hundred thousand rupees" — i.e. Rs 100,000 to Rs 500,000.

- Under [082/2026 §90(1)], the master, captain or agent must notify an Immigration Officer where a transit passenger or crew member fails to continue their journey and it may "reasonably be inferred" they remained in Sri Lanka.
- Failure to comply is an offence under [082/2026 §90(2)], with the master, captain or agent "jointly and severally liable on conviction" to that fine range.
- The same range applies to related reporting offences, e.g. aircraft lists under [082/2026 §85(3)].

Caveats: This is the Immigration Bill (Bill, 2026-10-07); §90 text is noted as identical in 508/2024, 513/2024 and 071/2026. The extracted [508/2024] text stops before the equivalent provision.

question: Under the proposed Convention against Doping in Sport amendment, how long does the Board Chairman serve?
answer:
Three years, with eligibility for reappointment, under the 2025 amendment bill.

- New section 14(2) provides the Chairman "shall hold office for a term of three years and shall be eligible for reappointment" [636/2025 §11].
- The Chairman is one of the appointed members, chosen by the Minister on the recommendation of the majority of ex-officio members [636/2025 §11].
- The earlier principal enactment (2013) had the same three-year term [046/2013 §14].

Caveats: this is the Bill version (12.09.2025); no Gazette version or committee-stage amendments are in the evidence.

question: Under the amended Rubber Control Act, who is defined as the “Director‑General”?
answer:
The amended Act defines “Director‑General” as “the Director‑General of the Rubber Development Department, appointed or deemed to have been appointed under this Act” [595/2025 §6] (identical text in [620/2025]). This replaces the repealed definition of “Controller” in section 52 of the principal enactment [595/2025 §6].

- Every reference to “Controller”/“Rubber Controller” in the Act becomes “Director‑General” [595/2025 §2]; elsewhere it reads as “Director‑General of the Rubber Development Department” [595/2025 §2(2)].

Caveats: The newest text is Bill 620/2025 (2025‑07‑09); the GS version 595/2025 is dated 2025‑05‑28, and the quoted clause is identical in both.

question: In the amended Personal Data Protection Act, which bodies are regarded as a public authority?
answer:
The evidence does not contain the definition of “public authority”, so I cannot say which bodies are regarded as such. The definitions passage [152/2021 §47] runs alphabetically from “anonymise” to “financial data” and is truncated before reaching “public authority”.

- The term is used but not defined in the passages: “Where a controller or a processor is a Public Authority, a single Data Protection Officer may be designated for several such public authorities” [152/2021 §20(3)].
- Separately, a DPO is required where processing is by “a ministry, government department or public corporation, except for judiciary acting in their judicial capacity” [152/2021 §20(1)(a)] — this is a DPO trigger, not a definition of public authority.
- Public authorities are barred from processing personal data in a third country save under an adequacy decision [152/2021 §26(1)].

Caveats: The interpretation section (§47) is incomplete here; the missing definition is needed to answer, and note the corpus version is the 2021 GS, with identical text in 167/2022.

question: What criteria does the amendment set for a crop to be classified as an Export Agricultural Crop?
answer:
Under the amendment to s.19, an "Export Agricultural Crop" is any crop "identified as a crop that have an export potential in addition to the local consumption" — excluding paddy, vegetables, fruits, root crops and other food crops — that the Minister declares "a notified agricultural crop" under section 2 [045/2026 §5].

- It "shall not include any crop identified as a plantation crop" [045/2026 §5].
- The same text appears in Bill 060/2026 (presented 2026-08-07); the version quoted is the GS of 2026-06-25 [045/2026 §5].

Caveats: Only the GS text of §5 is given verbatim; the Bill 060/2026 clause text is not reproduced, so an identical wording is inferred from the matching outline.

question: Under the proposed Chiththa Advanced Psychological Studies Open Institute of Sri Lanka law, what does the term “qualified auditor” refer to?
answer:
Under the Chiththa bill [597/2025 §10(4)], "qualified auditor" means either an individual, or a firm whose resident partners each qualify, holding membership of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka (or another institute established by law) and "a certificate to practice as an Accountant" issued by that institute's Council.

- Appointment: the auditor is appointed by the Auditor General "in terms of Article 154 of the Constitution" [597/2025 §10(3)].
- Two limbs: (a) an individual member with a practising certificate; or (b) a firm of accountants where each resident partner is such a member with a practising certificate [597/2025 §10(4)].

Caveats: This is the Gazette version (GS, 2025-05-29), stated to be identical in 608/2025; no presented Bill text is in evidence.

question: Under the proposed Proceeds of Crime Bill, what types of advanced investigative methods can an investigation officer employ with a magistrate’s permission?
answer:
Under the Proceeds of Crime Bill, with a Magistrate’s authorization under section 56, an investigation officer may use controlled delivery, digital surveillance, undercover operations, traps, and forensic extraction from digital devices [570/2025 §60; 572/2025 §56].

- “Digital surveillance” expressly includes “interception and recording of digital, voice, video communication”; undercover operations may use “decoys” [570/2025 §60].
- The Magistrate must consider “necessity and justification” and “proportionality,” and may impose conditions [570/2025 §60].
- The officer must report progress to the Magistrate “once in fourteen days” [570/2025 §60].

Caveat: the §60 text is identical in the GS (570/2025) and Bill (572/2025) versions.

question: Under the proposed Chartered Institute of Media Professionals of Sri Lanka law, how many council members must be present, and must the Chairperson be among them, to constitute a quorum for a council meeting?
answer:
Five members, and the Chairperson must be one of them: the quorum is "ﬁve members including the Chairperson" [054/2026 §7(2)].

- The same wording appears in the earlier Gazette version, so the GS and Bill texts do not differ on this point [040/2026 §7(2)].
- Relatedly, the Chairperson presides at every Council meeting, with the Vice-Chairperson presiding if absent [054/2026 §7(5)].

Caveats: The newest text I relied on is titled "Establishment of the Chartered Institute of Media" (Bill, 2026-07-22), not exactly "Chartered Institute of Media Professionals of Sri Lanka"; the GS version (2026-06-05) carries that fuller title and is identical here.

question: Under the National Transport Commission amendment, what steps must the Commission and transport operators follow to set and show fares for bus and other transport services?
answer:
The amendment inserts a new section 38A: fares are computed by the Commission under a formula it determines, "adhering to the national policy relating to transportation fares approved by Parliament", and specified by Gazette Order [592/2025 §19 §38A(1)].

- The Commission publishes fare lists on its official website; each provider must prepare its own list "in accordance with such lists" and display it "at any conspicuous place of the transportation vehicle" [592/2025 §19 §38A(2)].
- The Commission may inspect compliance under section 39(2), and failure "shall be guilty of an offence under section 40" [592/2025 §19 §38A(3)].
- Same text appears in the GS version [577/2025 §19] and in [549/2024 §19], so the versions do not differ on this clause.

Caveats: the penalties under section 40, the formula itself, and any detail on how electronic fare display is regulated (see regulation-making power in [577/2025 §24]) are not set out in these passages.

question: According to the proposed Mass Foundation law, what continuous legal identity will the foundation have, what ability does it have to bring or face lawsuits, how can it manage its seal, and how is it classified for regulatory oversight?
answer:
Under the Mass Foundation (Incorporation) bill the body corporate has "perpetual succession" under the name "Mass Foundation", with power to "sue and be sued" [025/2026 §2].

- Seal: it may "have and use a common seal and to alter the same at its pleasure" [025/2026 §2]; the seal is affixed only "in the presence of two members of the Committee" who sign the instrument, and is kept in the custody of an office bearer the Committee decides [025/2026 §15].
- Oversight: it is "deemed to be a Voluntary Social Service Organization" under the Voluntary Social Service Organizations (Registration and Supervision) Act, No. 31 of 1980, which governs its affairs [025/2026 §2].

Caveats: The same text appears in Bill 037/2026 (presented 2026-05-07); the clauses cited are from the GS version 025/2026 (2026-04-08), which is stated to be identical.

question: Under the amendment to the National Water Supply and Drainage Board Law, when a water supply and sewerage undertaking of an industrial park is transferred to the Board, which minister is treated as the ‘Minister in charge of the subject of Local Government’ for applying Part III of the Act?
answer:
For an industrial estate or industrial park, the phrase "the Minister in charge of the subject of Local Government" in Part III is read as **the Minister assigned the subject of the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka (under the Board of Investment Law No. 4 of 1978), under Article 44 or 45 of the Constitution, or the Minister assigned the subject of industries under Article 44 or 45 — "as the case may be"** [053/2026 §10].

- This is new section 57a, inserted after section 57 of the principal enactment [053/2026 §10].
- The text is identical in the earlier Bill [019/2026 §10, 2026-03-13]; the newer version is [053/2026, 2026-07-21].

Caveats: The provision does not say which of the two ministers prevails where both exist — it uses "as the case may be." The community-based-organization rule in proviso (b) is separate and not covered here.

question: Under the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill, what responsibilities does a magistrate have when an approved detention centre lies within his jurisdiction?
answer:
Under the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill (078/2026, Bill, 2026-10-06 — title matches the question), the magistrate for the area must inspect the centre **once a month**, without advance notice to its authority [078/2026 §33(1)].

- Must "visit once a month", "interview the suspects and look into their well-being", and "call for and inspect detention registers, Detention Orders and other books and documents" [078/2026 §33(1)(a)–(c)].
- On observing or being told of torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment, must "forthwith" order production before a Judicial Medical Officer and obtain the report [078/2026 §33(4)]; if satisfied on reasonable grounds, he "shall act in terms of section 31" [078/2026 §33(5); §31].
- Non-conforming conditions at inspection must be reported to the Inspector General of Police [078/2026 §34(2)].

Caveats: The 2024 Anti Terrorism Bill instead requires a **weekly** visit by the magistrate before whom the suspect was produced [444/2024 §32(1)(a)] — a different bill; the identical text also appears in 070/2026.

question: Under the Mediation (Civil and Commercial Disputes) Bill, which civil or commercial disagreements can be taken to mediation and which types are excluded from this law?
answer:
The Bill applies to "civil and commercial disputes" settled by mediation — whether under a mediation agreement, voluntarily referred by a party, or referred by a court [622/2025 §2(1)]; disputes under the Mediation Boards Act and the Special Categories Act are carved out.

- Expressly excluded: disputes mediable under the Mediation Boards Act, No. 72 of 1988, or the Mediation (Special Categories of Disputes) Act, No. 21 of 2003 — which must not be submitted under this Act [622/2025 §2(2)–(3)].
- The newest text is Bill 622/2025 (11 July 2025); identical wording appears in GS 616/2025 (3 July 2025) [622/2025 §2; 616/2025].

Caveats: §3 ("A mediation shall not be conducted in respect of any dispute…") and a heading "Disputes that cannot be mediated" [622/2025 §5] appear in the outline, but their full text is not in the evidence, so any further exclusions cannot be stated.

question: What audit regulations govern the financial statements of Samurdhi community‑based banking societies under the Samurdhi amendment?
answer:
Under the amendment, the accounts of Samurdhi community-based banking societies are audited under the rules for public corporations: new section 35A applies Article 154 of the Constitution and the National Audit Act, No. 19 of 2018 [600/2025 §3]. The same text appears in the presented Bill [614/2025 §3].

- Section 35A is inserted immediately after section 35 of the principal enactment (Samurdhi Act, No. 1 of 2013) [600/2025 §3].
- A parallel section 28A applies the same two audit frameworks to Samurdhi community-based banks [600/2025 §2].
- No new penalties are introduced; the text creates an audit obligation only [600/2025 bill-level description].

Caveats: The GS (2025-06-04) and Bill (2025-06-17) texts are stated to be identical; no committee-stage amendments are in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed Companies (Amendment) Act, what remedy is available to a company whose name has been struck off, and what are the effects on its former assets?
answer:
Yes — the evidence supports an answer, drawn from the amendment to section 487(5) of the Companies Act: the struck-off company may apply to court within ten years, and on re-registration the court may order return of its property.

- Remedy: apply to court "before the expiry of a period of ten years", making the "Attorney-General a party", showing cause why it could not comply with subsection (1); the court may then "permit the re-registration of the company" [582/2025 §17].
- Assets: property previously "shall vest in and be at the disposal of the State", and the court may "make an order for the return to the company of all property previously vested in the State" [582/2025 §17].
- Limits: rights of third parties who acquired the property from the State "in good faith" are unaffected; the State is not liable where property is destroyed, damaged, or never physically taken [582/2025 §17].

Newest text: 582/2025 (GS, 2024-04-24 — actually 2025-04-24), identical to 606/2025; the 2024 bill 541/2024 §15 has the same scheme, differing only in the commencement wording ("coming into operation of this amendment Act").

Caveats: the ten-year period runs from the Act's date of operation, so the deadline is not yet fixed; the 2023 and 2018 bills (406/2023, 531/2018) concern different subjects and do not address restoration.

question: Under the revised Anti‑Corruption Act, in what situations will a person charged with a corruption offence be refused bail?
answer:
Under the 2026 amendment to s.149, bail is refused — "except in exceptional circumstances by a High Court" — only where the Director-General certifies the value thresholds are met: a bribe of "not less than one hundred thousand rupees", a loss to the Government of "not less than five hundred thousand rupees", or a gain/benefit of that amount [063/2026 §17 (Bill, 2026-08-19); identical in 051/2026 §17 (GS, 2026-07-27)].

- Otherwise all offences are "cognizable and non-bailable as per the provisions of the Bail Act, No. 30 of 1997" [063/2026 §17].
- The existing s.149(1) (Anti-Corruption Bill 319/2023, 2023-04-27, §149) instead required the Magistrate to "remand such person until the conclusion of the trial", with bail only in "exceptional circumstances and for reasons to be recorded".

Caveats: this is an amendment Bill, not the consolidated Act; the evidence gives threshold-based criteria, not a list of "situations". 063/2026 §17 contains garbled wording ("offering of section 149… a bribe").

question: Under the proposed Prevention of Foreign Terrorist Fighters law, how are offences listed in Part B of the extradition schedule treated when Sri Lanka considers extraditing a suspect to another UN member state?
answer:
They are deemed **not** to be offences of a political character — so the political-offence exception cannot block extradition. [073/2026 §11]

- The deeming applies "notwithstanding anything in the Extradition Law, No. 8 of 1977", and covers a political offence, an offence connected with one, or one "inspired by political motives". [073/2026 §11]
- It operates "for the purposes only of extradition" of a person accused or convicted of such an offence, as between Sri Lanka and any UN Member State, or for assistance under section 12. [073/2026 §11]
- §8 inserts the new Act's offences into the Extradition Law Schedule just before Part B. [073/2026 §8]

Caveats: Evidence is the Gazette version (2026-09-30), identical in 085/2026; the text of the Schedule's Part B itself is not reproduced.

question: Under the revised National Environmental Act, what monetary penalty does a person face if convicted of an offence covered by Section 23r, and what extra daily charge applies if the violation persists after the conviction?
answer:
Under the National Environmental Bill, a conviction under amended Section 23r carries a fine of "not less than one hundred thousand rupees and not more than one million rupees", plus "a fine of five thousand rupees for each day" the offence continues after conviction. [032/2026 §18]

- The fine is imposed "on conviction before the Magistrate having jurisdiction". [032/2026 §18]
- These replace the earlier range of ten thousand to one hundred thousand rupees, and five hundred rupees per day. [032/2026 §18]

Caveats: The evidence is a Bill (2026-05-06); the same text appears in 026/2026, and the title reads "National Environmental", not "National Environmental Act".

question: What penalty does the amendment to the National Audit Act impose for the offence covered by Section 42?
answer:
The amendment replaces the old fine band with a fine "not exceeding one hundred thousand rupees" or imprisonment "of either description for a term not exceeding one year", or both [611/2025 §13].

- Section 42's previous wording — "a fine not less than five thousand rupees and not more than twenty five thousand rupees" — is substituted [611/2025 §13].
- The same Gazette bill makes a separate, heavier change to Section 43(1): up to three years' imprisonment [611/2025 §14].

Caveats: This is the Gazette version (GS, 2025-06-23); the presented Bill text is not in the evidence, and the offence itself is defined in the principal enactment, not quoted here.

question: Under the proposed Elimination of Rabies and Registration of Dogs law, what fine and additional action apply if a dog owner does not vaccinate and register the dog after being given a notice?
answer:
A Rs 2,000 penalty is payable, in addition to the registration fee under section 5, and the local authority must itself vaccinate and register the dog immediately in the Register of Dogs [076/2026 §7(4); identical in 066/2026 §7(4)].

- The trigger is failure to vaccinate or register "within the specified time limits" — normally 14 days from the authorised officer's notice, extendable by a further 14 days for reasonable cause [076/2026 §7(2)–(3)].
- The fee referred to is the prescribed registration fee paid on registration under section 5 [066/2026 §5(1)], with the entry made in the Register of Dogs kept under section 8 [066/2026 §8].

Caveats: The text appears in both the GS (066/2026, 2026-09-07) and the presented Bill (076/2026, 2026-09-24) in identical terms; no committee-stage amendments are included.

question: Under the proposed amendment to Sri Lanka’s drug control law, how is the list of named narcotics changed and what new penalty is introduced for manufacturing other listed dangerous drugs?
answer:
The newest text, the Poisons, Opium and Dangerous Drugs (Amendment) Bill (068/2026, 2026-09-08; the Gazette version 062/2026 of 2026-08-24 is identical on this point), adds **methamphetamine** to the named narcotics and creates a new offence for manufacturing other listed drugs.

- Section 54A(1)(a) substitutes "heroin, cocaine, morphine, opium or methamphetamine" for "heroin or cocaine or morphine or opium" [068/2026 §2].
- New paragraph (aa) covers manufacturing "any dangerous drug set out in Groups A, B, C, D and E in Part I of the Third Schedule" other than those five, tried by the High Court without a jury [068/2026 §2].
- Penalty: fine "not less than two hundred thousand rupees and not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees", or "imprisonment ... not less than ten years and not exceeding twenty years", or both [068/2026 §2].

Caveats: the evidence does not reproduce the Groups A–E Schedule entries themselves, so the full list of "other" drugs cannot be verified; the Cannabis additions appear only in the Gazette version [062/2026 §5].

question: Under the proposed Presidents' Entitlements repeal, will former presidents or their widows keep receiving housing, regular payments, secretarial assistance, official transport or a widow's pension once the new law takes effect?
answer:
No. The repeal Bill expressly ends those benefits: once it commences, former Presidents and widows of former Presidents stop receiving them.

- Residence provided or monthly allowance paid cease "on and after the date of commencement" [624/2025 §3(a)].
- Monthly secretarial allowance, official transport and "such other facilities" also cease [624/2025 §3(b)].
- The widow's monthly pension ceases likewise [624/2025 §3(c)], with the 1986 Act repealed outright [624/2025 §2].

Caveats: The Gazette version (624/2025, 31 Jul 2025) and presented Bill (627/2025, 7 Aug 2025) are stated to be identical here; amounts and commencement date are not in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Penal Code, what new penalty is introduced for intentionally causing serious injury to a child under 18?
answer:
The bill inserts a new section 316a creating an offence of voluntarily causing **grievous hurt** to a person under eighteen: imprisonment of either description up to **ten years**, plus liability to a fine and possible court-ordered compensation [618/2025 §6].

- The offence is expressed as "voluntarily causes grievous hurt," not "intentionally"; the text also retains the exception for the case provided for by section 326 [618/2025 §6].
- Compensation is fixed by the court after considering a victim impact statement from the National Authority for the Protection of Victims of Crime and Witnesses under Act No. 10 of 2023 [618/2025 §6].
- The same clause appears in Bill 630/2025 (Bill, 2025-08-19), the presented version of the GS bill 618/2025 (2025-07-08) [630/2025].

Caveats: The evidence gives no clause text expressly using "intentionally" for this offence; that wording appears only in the auto-generated summary of the "wilfully"/"intentionally" change to section 308a.

question: How does the proposed amendment to the Social Security Contribution Levy Act change the turnover limits and the applicable dates in Section 5, and what new limit is introduced for periods starting on 1 April 2026?
answer:
The amendment (GS 017/2026, 2026-03-03; same clause text in Bill 023/2026, 2026-03-17) restates Section 5(1)(b)–(c) and adds a new paragraph (d) setting the four-quarter limit at "thirty-six million rupees" from 1 April 2026 [017/2026 §3].

- Para (b): "hundred and twenty million rupees; or" becomes "hundred and twenty million rupees;" — the "or" is dropped [017/2026 §3(1)].
- Para (c): the period is narrowed to "on or after January 1, 2024 and prior to April 1, 2026," and "sixty million rupees." becomes "sixty million rupees; or" [017/2026 §3(2)].
- New para (d): "for any period commencing on or after April 1, 2026," turnover over "consecutive four quarters" must "not exceed thirty-six million rupees" [017/2026 §3(3)].

Caveats: the quoted clause text is the only source for this change; no consolidated Section 5 text is in the evidence, so verify the final wording against the Bill.

question: What changes does the amendment to Section 14 of the Sri Lanka Electricity Act make to the ownership percentage requirement and to the type of entities mentioned in its subsections?
answer:
The amendment raises the ownership threshold in Section 14(1) from “more than fifty per centum” to “one hundred per centum”, and replaces “person” references in subsections (2) and (3) with a company incorporated under the Companies Act, No. 07 of 2007 [584/2025 §12].

- Section 14(1): “more than fifty per centum” → “one hundred per centum” [584/2025 §12].
- Section 14(2): “Any person who” → “Any company incorporated in terms of the Companies Act, No. 07 of 2007, which” [584/2025 §12].
- Section 14(3): “a person who” → “a company, which” [584/2025 §12].

Caveats: The evidence quotes only the substitutions, not the full amended subsections; the text is from the GS bill dated 2025-05-16, also stated identical in 599/2025 [584/2025 §12].

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Trusts Ordinance, which part of Section 3 is being removed and how is the definition of “express trust” being changed?
answer:
Paragraph (n) of Section 3 of the Trusts Ordinance (Cap. 87) is repealed, and in paragraph (p) the definition of “express trust” is changed by substituting “trust in the form” for “trust generally in the form” [081/2026 §2].

- This is the Trusts (Amendment) bill, GS version dated 2026-10-14 (identical text in 086/2026) [081/2026 §2].
- The amendment is expressed as a further amendment to Section 3 as last amended by Act No. 6 of 2018 [081/2026 §2].

Caveats: The evidence does not reproduce the text of paragraph (n) or the full definition, so the practical effect of removing (n) cannot be stated.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Judicature Act, how are the retirement ages for judges and magistrates being changed?
answer:
Under the amendment, the retirement age for certain judges rises from **61 to 63**, while "all other Judges and Magistrates" retire at **62** — the latter expressly overriding the Public and Judicial Officers (Retirement) Ordinance (Chapter 355) [058/2026 §3(1)–(2)].

- Substitution of "sixty-one years" with "sixty-three years" in section 6(3) [058/2026 §3(1)].
- Repeal and replacement of section 6(4) fixing "sixty-two years" for all other Judges and Magistrates [058/2026 §3(2)].

Caveats: the clause text is from the GS version (058/2026, 2026-08-07); the presented Bill (064/2026, 2026-08-18) is recorded as carrying identical text, so no difference appears. "Certain judges" is the clause's own scope, not a list I can supply from this evidence.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Universities Act, how many terms is a person allowed to serve as dean of a faculty?
answer:
No more than **two terms** as Dean of a Faculty: “No person shall be appointed as the Dean of a Faculty for more than two terms.” [649/2025 §2]

- The same text appears in the newest version, Universities (Amendment) Bill **655/2025** (Bill, 2025-12-03), and in GS **649/2025** (2025-11-21). [649/2025 §2]

question: What 2025 legislation establishes the professional facilities‑management institute as a legal corporate body in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The **Institute of Facilities Management Sri Lanka (Incorporation) Bill** — **Bill 628/2025**, presented **6 August 2025** (GS version **623/2025**, 18 July 2025) — creates the Institute as a body corporate [623/2025].

- Clause 2(1): members “shall have perpetual succession under the name and style of the ‘Institute of Facilities Management Sri Lanka’” [623/2025].
- The body corporate may “sue and be sued,” use a common seal, and do things incidental to a body corporate [623/2025].
- It must represent members’ majority interests and uphold professional standards [623/2025].

Caveat: the evidence shows Bill/GS versions, not an enacted Act number or commencement date.

question: Which 2025 legislation creates a legal corporation for the charitable foundation named after senior monk Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero?
answer:
Bill 596/2025, the Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero Suwasevana Foundation (Incorporation) Bill, presented on 2025-05-08 [596/2025 §2]. An earlier Gazette version, 581/2025, was published 2025-04-10 [581/2025].

- §2 vests members as a "body corporate with perpetual succession" able to sue, be sued and use a common seal [596/2025 §2].
- Short title: the "...Foundation (Incorporation) Act, No. of 2025" [596/2025 §1].
- Both versions contain identical incorporation wording; no substantive difference is shown in the evidence [581/2025 §2].

Caveats: The evidence does not confirm enactment or a bill number; §1 leaves the Act number blank.

question: What 2026 amendment revises the Act that governs marriage and divorce among the Kandyan community (Chapter 113)?
answer:
The 2026 amendment is the **Kandyan Marriage and Divorce (Amendment)** bill: presented version 016/2026 (Bill, 19 Feb 2026), preceded by 008/2026 (GS, 5 Feb 2026); both amend the Kandyan Marriage and Divorce Act (Chapter 113).

- Clause 2 replaces section 32(a) with "Adultery by the husband or wife after marrige." and repeals paragraph (b) [008/2026 §2].
- Short title: "Kandyan Marriage and Divorce (Amendment) Act, No. of 2026" [008/2026 §1].
- Presented by Hon. (Mrs.) Rohini Kumari Wijerathna, M.P. [016/2026].

Caveats: No passage gives an Act number or states that this 2026 bill has been enacted; the "adultery" summary wording comes from auto-generated descriptions, though §2's text confirms it.

question: What is the 2026 legislation that establishes the Al‑Hashimi Association as a legal corporate entity?
answer:
The **Al‑Hashimi Association (Incorporation) Bill** — Bill 039/2026, presented 21 May 2026 — with its earlier Gazette version, 024/2026 (GS, 8 April 2026). Both contain identical text here.

- §2(1) constitutes existing and future members as a body corporate "under the name and style of the 'Al‑Hashimi Association'", with "perpetual succession", power to sue and be sued, and a common seal [024/2026 §2].
- It is deemed a Voluntary Social Service Organization under Act No. 31 of 1980, whose provisions apply to its management [024/2026 §2].
- Objects include helping poor people and students, youth self‑employment, fund‑raising and a trust to manage assets [024/2026 §3].

Caveats: Committee‑stage amendments are not in this corpus; no penalties are specified in the evidence.

question: Which 2026 bill repeals the 2009 act that created the position of chief of the defence staff in Sri Lanka?
answer:
Bill 059/2026, the Chief of Defence Staff (Repeal) Bill (Bill, 2026-08-04): clause 2 states "The Chief of Defence Staff Act, No. 35 of 2009 is hereby repealed" [059/2026 §2].

- Earlier version: the same repeal appears as Gazette bill 036/2026 (GS, 2026-05-15); the quoted clause text is noted as identical in both [059/2026 §2].
- Effect: holders of the offices of Chief of Defence Staff and Committee member "shall cease to hold such office" from commencement [059/2026 §3].
- Short title: "Chief of Defence Staff (Repeal) Act, No. of 2026" [059/2026 §1].

question: What 2025 legislation modifies the 1988 Provincial Councils Elections Act in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The match is Bill 605/2025, **Provincial Councils Elections (Amendment)** (presented 5 June 2025; earlier Gazette version 589/2025, 22 May 2025), which amends the Provincial Councils Elections Act, No. 2 of 1988.

- §2 restores the 1988 Act "in force on September 21, 2017", "notwithstanding the amendments made thereto by Act, No. 17 of 2017", operative from the Act's coming into force, saving acts done from 22 September 2017 that are not inconsistent with the 1988 Act [589/2025 §2; identical in 605/2025].
- §3: in any Sinhala–Tamil inconsistency, "the Sinhala text shall prevail" [589/2025 §3; also 605/2025].
- Short title: "Provincial Councils Elections (Amendment) Act, No. of 2025" — number left blank [605/2025 §1].

Caveats: Evidence is incomplete — apart from §§1–3 the operative amendment provisions are not shown, and no enactment number or certificate of enactment appears, so I cannot confirm it became law or list specific changes to the 1988 Act.

question: Which 2025 bill amends the 2016 Act that provides a financial assistance scheme for workers?
answer:
The matching 2025 bill is the **Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers (Amendment) Bill 602/2025** (Bill, 3 June 2025); an earlier GS version is **587/2025** (20 May 2025). Both amend the **Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers Act, No. 4 of 2016** [602/2025 §2].

- It amends section 3 to set allowance periods ending “March 31, 2025” [602/2025 §2].
- The Bill is deemed to have come into operation on “April 1, 2025” [602/2025 §1].

Caveats: “financial assistance scheme” is my reading of the Budgetary Relief Allowance; the evidence does not use that exact phrase.

question: Which 2025 bill seeks to amend the 2016 legislation that establishes the minimum wage for employees in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The newest is **Bill 604/2025, National Minimum Wage of Workers (Amendment) — Bill (2025-06-03)**; it amends section 3 of the **National Minimum Wage of Workers Act, No. 3 of 2016** [604/2025 §2]. The same text also appears in **GS 586/2025 (2025-05-20)** [586/2025].

- It sets the monthly minimum at “twenty-seven thousand rupees” for 1 Apr–31 Dec 2025, rising to “thirty thousand rupees” from 1 Jan 2026 [604/2025 §2].
- Budgetary relief allowances are declared part of the minimum wage [604/2025 §3].
- The Act is deemed to commence on 1 April 2025 [604/2025 §1].

Caveat: 604/2025 is the presented Bill; 586/2025 is the earlier Gazette version.

question: Which 2025 amendment alters the 2005 law that established the workers' special financial assistance allowance?
answer:
The 2025 amendment is the **Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers (Amendment)** bill, which amends the Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers Act, No. 36 of 2005 — the name in the question is a paraphrase; the Act's title uses "Budgetary Relief Allowance." The presented Bill is 603/2025 (2025-06-03); the earlier Gazette version is 588/2025 (2025-05-20).

- It substitutes "With effect from August 1, 2005" in section 3(1) with "For the period commencing on August 1, 2005 and ending on March 31, 2025" [588/2025 §2; identical text in 603/2025].
- Sinhala text prevails over Tamil in any inconsistency [588/2025 §3].

Caveats: The summary is auto-generated and describes only a change in the allowance's period; no powers, offences or penalties are created. A separate bill (587/2025) similarly amends the 2016 Act, No. 4 of 2016.

question: What 2026 legislation proposes to abolish the 1977 law that provided retirement benefits to Sri Lankan parliamentarians?
answer:
Bill 001/2026, the Parliamentary Pensions (Repeal) Bill (Bill, 2026-01-07), which states: "The Parliamentary Pensions Law, No. 1 of 1977 is hereby repealed" [001/2026 §2].

- Title/date: cited as the Parliamentary Pensions (Repeal); presented by the Minister of Justice and National Integration [001/2026 §1].
- Effect per the bill-level summary (auto-generated hint): it also stops pensions received under that 1977 law or related provisions of the 1982 and 1990 Acts, and creates no new powers or penalties [001/2026].
- §3 addresses "avoidance of doubt" on existing pension payments; the full wording is truncated in the evidence [001/2026 §3].

Caveats: §3's exact text is cut off, so its precise effect on existing payments can't be confirmed from clause text alone.
warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 001/2026 §1, 001/2026 §3

question: Which 2025 bill sought to modify the 1988 Sri Lankan law that imposes a tax on gambling activities?
answer:
The **Betting and Gaming Levy (Amendment) Bill 642/2025** (Bill, 21 Oct 2025) sought to amend the **Betting and Gaming Levy Act, No. 40 of 1988**; an earlier Gazette version is **640/2025** (GS, 2 Oct 2025) [642/2025] [640/2025 §2].

- The GS clause amends section 2 of the 1988 Act “as last amended by Act, No. 11 of 2023” [640/2025 §2].
- It sets “fifteen per centum” for years from 1 Apr 2023 but ending before 1 Oct 2025, and “eighteen per centum” from 1 Oct 2025 [640/2025 §2].
- It raises the specified amount from “United States Dollars fifty” to “United States Dollars one hundred” [640/2025 §2].

Caveat: the presented Bill’s clause text is not in evidence; only its outline and the GS text are provided.

question: Which 2025 bill proposes changes to the Land Development Ordinance (Chapter 464)?
answer:
Two 2025 bills amend the **Land Development Ordinance (Chapter 464)**: the newest is **Bill 625/2025** (presented 22 July 2025), preceded by **GS 617/2025** (4 July 2025). Both have the same short title, “Land Development (Amendment) Act” [617/2025 §1; 625/2025].

- Bill 625/2025 removes “or upon his or her marriage” from section 48A(2)(c) [625/2025 §2].
- It changes section 68(1) from “fails to succeed” to “fails without reasonable cause to succeed” [625/2025 §4].
- GS 617/2025 repeals section 48B(1)(a) [617/2025 §3]; the evidence says this text is identical in 625/2025.

Caveats: The evidence gives only excerpts, not a full version comparison.

question: Which 2026 bill updates the 2018 Finance Act No. 35?
answer:
The **Finance (Amendment) Bill, No. 034/2026** (presented 2026-05-06) — preceded by the Gazette version **027/2026** (2026-04-23) — amends section 44 of the Finance Act, No. 35 of 2018 [034/2026 §2] [027/2026].

- It substitutes text in s.44(1) to add a proviso: the levy "shall not be charged" for a newly constructed cellular tower commencing commercial operations "on or after January 1, 2026," for "a period of five years" [034/2026 §2].
- It also amends s.44(2), substituting "The levy shall be paid" with "Subject to the provisions of subsection (1), the levy shall be paid" [034/2026 §2].
- §3 addresses Sinhala/Tamil inconsistency, with the Sinhala prevailing [034/2026] [034/2026 §3 outline].

Caveats: Both versions share identical clause text; no committee-stage amendments are in this corpus, and the Bill's number/title differs slightly from the GS version's.
warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 034/2026 §3

question: Which 2026 bill revises the 1956 law that sets rules for female workers, teenage employees and child labor?
answer:
Bill 056/2026 — the Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children (Amendment) Bill (22 July 2026) — amends Act No. 47 of 1956, which governs the employment of women, young persons and children [056/2026 §1].

- It substitutes "one hundred thousand rupees" for "ten thousand rupees" in sections 7(3), 13(2) and 20a(3) [056/2026 §2; §3; §4].
- The higher fines do not apply to offences committed before the amendment comes into operation [056/2026 §5].
- An earlier Gazette version, 044/2026 (GS, 25 June 2026), carries identical clause text [044/2026 §6].

Caveats: the 044/2026 entries are marked as having identical text; only the 056/2026 presented Bill is summarised in detail.

question: Which 2025 bill proposes to revoke the 2024 legislation that introduced internet safety and content regulation measures?
answer:
The Online Safety (Repeal) bill: the Gazette version 578/2025 (GS, 2025-04-08) and the presented version 590/2025 (Bill, 2025-05-08), whose texts are identical on this point. It states: "The Online Safety Act, No. 9 of 2024 is hereby repealed" [578/2025 §2].

- It also repeals regulations made under the 2024 Act, "from the date of enactment of this Act" [590/2025 §3].
- Short title: "Online Safety (Repeal) Act, No. of 2025" [590/2025 §1].

Caveats: Committee-stage amendments are not in this corpus.

question: What 2025 legislation addresses re‑conducting postponed local council elections by allowing new nominations and setting a fresh election date?
answer:
The **Local Authorities Elections (Special Provisions)** bill — Gazette version [565/2025] (2025-01-01) and the presented Bill [566/2025] (2025-01-09); the cited clause text is identical in both.

- It voids earlier nomination papers for the listed authorities, treating them "as if such nomination papers had never been submitted" [565/2025 §2(1)].
- Fresh nomination notices under s.26 of the Ordinance must be published on a date the Election Commission determines, "not later than three months from the date of coming into operation of this Act" [565/2025 §3].
- Deposits by party or independent candidates are to be refunded on production of the receipt [565/2025 §2(3)].

Caveats: The evidence does not state the actual fresh election date, only the three-month deadline for nomination notices; it also does not confirm enactment.

question: Which 2025 bill updates the 2008 act that governs major strategic development projects in Sri Lanka?
answer:
Bill 650/2025, the Strategic Development Projects (Amendment) Bill presented on 2025-11-14, amends the Strategic Development Projects Act, No. 14 of 2008; the identical Gazette version is 643/2025 (GS, 2025-11-07) [650/2025 §2] [643/2025].

- It substitutes "ten years" for the existing "twenty-five years" in section 2 of the 2008 Act, as last amended by Act No. 12 of 2011 [650/2025 §2].
- It replaces section 3, requiring the Board of Investment to identify projects and refer them to the Ministry of Finance for "ex-ante cost-benefit analysis", with a recommendation due "within one month" [650/2025 §3].
- The Minister must publish a Gazette Order, "with the concurrence of the Cabinet of Ministers", specifying the project and its exemptions, to be "placed before Parliament for information" [650/2025 §3].

Caveats: Committee-stage amendments are not in this corpus; the two versions' clause text is stated to be identical.

question: Which 2026 bill was introduced to legally establish the UnV charitable foundation?
answer:
The **UnV Foundation (Incorporation) Bill** — published as Gazette bill **003/2026 (GS, 9 January 2026)** and presented to Parliament as **010/2026 (Bill, 22 January 2026)**, whose texts are stated to be identical [010/2026 §1] [003/2026].

- It is "An Act to incorporate the UnV Foundation", a foundation already "heretofore established in Sri Lanka" [010/2026] [003/2026].
- Incorporated as a body corporate with perpetual succession, classed as a Voluntary Social Service Organization under Act No. 31 of 1980 [003/2026].

Caveats: The described objects come from an auto-generated summary; the full clause text of §2–§3 is not in the evidence.

question: Which 2025 bill updates Sri Lanka's 1979 criminal procedure legislation?
answer:
The 2025 bill is **576/2025, Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment) – GS**, published **2025-03-28**, amending the **Code of Criminal Procedure Act, No. 15 of 1979** [576/2025 §2]. The evidence states the same text also appears in **579/2025** [576/2025 §2].

- It inserts new sections **144A and 144B** on dispensing with a suspect/accused’s personal court attendance [576/2025 §2].
- It inserts new sections **273A–273U**, including remote audio-visual witness evidence [576/2025 §5].
- It amends the Second Schedule by adding **Forms 24 and 25** [576/2025 §6].

question: What 2026 bill proposes the twenty‑second revision of Sri Lanka’s constitution?
answer:
Bill 065/2026, the **Twenty Second Amendment to the Constitution** (presented version, 18 August 2026); an earlier Gazette version is 057/2026 (7 August 2026) [065/2026] [057/2026].

- Short title: "This Act may be cited as the Twenty Second Amendment to the Constitution" [057/2026 §1].
- It amends only Article 107 (retirement: Supreme Court 67, Court of Appeal 65, Chief Justice at 67 or six years, whichever earlier) and Article 137 ("not more than nineteen" to "not more than twenty four other Judges") [065/2026 §2] [065/2026 §3].
- Both versions carry identical Article 107/137 and inconsistency-clause text; no textual difference is apparent in the evidence [065/2026 §3] [057/2026 §4].

Caveats: The bill-level summaries are auto-generated and one contains an error ("67 to 67"); clause text above governs. Committee-stage amendments are not covered.

question: Which 2026 bill seeks to repeal the 1972 Tenancy Act (No. 7) in Sri Lanka?
answer:
Bill 006/2026, the **Rent (Repeal) - Bill** (presented version, dated 2026-01-20), repeals the 1972 Act — though its §2 names it the "Rent Act, No. 7 of 1972", not a "Tenancy Act" [006/2026 §2].

- §2 states simply: "The Rent Act, No. 7 of 1972 is hereby repealed" [006/2026 §2].
- Transitional protections run "for a period of one year from the relevant date", e.g. no ejectment suits and no rent above the "authorised rent" [006/2026 §3(a)-(b)].
- Earlier GS versions of the same repeal (526/2024 and 555/2024, GS 2024-07-19) carry identical §2 text [526/2024 §2].

Caveats: The title in the question ("Tenancy Act") does not match the bill text; no 2026 bill using that title appears in the evidence.

question: What 2026 legislation creates a corporate entity for the Mahawilachchiya children’s education centre?
answer:
Bill 015/2026 (presented 2026-02-18) and its Gazette predecessor 011/2026 (GS, 2026-02-06) both incorporate the centre; the evidence records their text as identical [015/2026] [011/2026 §2].

- §2(1) admits existing members of the "Centre" into a body corporate "with perpetual succession" and power to sue, be sued and use a common seal [011/2026 §2].
- The incorporated name in 011/2026 §2 is "Mahawilachchiya Centre for Education for Children" — wording differs from the Bill title and from the 2024 bill 511/2024, which used "Mahawilachchiya Education Centre for Children" [011/2026 §2] [511/2024 §2].
- It is deemed a Voluntary Social Services Organization under Act No. 31 of 1980 [011/2026 §2(2)].

Caveats: 015/2026's clause text is not shown; identity with 011/2026 is per the evidence labels, and clause numbers may differ.
